name: Toyota Corolla
engine: 1.8L naturally-aspirated I4 (2ZR-FAE), 139 hp — 2.0L Dynamic Force I4 (M20A-FKS), 169 hp on SE/XSE — 1.8L hybrid, 121 hp combined
drivetrain: FWD (the hybrid added available AWD for 2023)
transmission: CVT (a Direct-Shift CVT with a physical launch gear on the 2.0L) · 6-speed manual offered on the 2.0L hatchback/SE · e-CVT on the hybrid
fuel_economy: 30 city / 38 hwy mpg (1.8L LE) · 31 / 40 (2.0L SE) · 53 / 52 (hybrid LE)
reliability: 9/10 — the Corolla is a benchmark for cheap, no-drama dependability. The 1.8L and 2.0L are port/direct-injection fours with timing chains, and the CVT is one of the more durable in the class, so these routinely pass 200k miles on basic maintenance. It is not fast, but almost nothing goes wrong. The main documented item is the 2020 Denso low-pressure fuel-pump recall that swept many Toyotas — have it confirmed complete on an affected car.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Low · Maintenance ~$350/yr (among the cheapest cars to keep) · Excellent fuel economy · Strong resale — the Corolla name sells itself on the used market
popular_mods: A quality set of all-season or winter tires — the single best upgrade on a light FWD commuter
All-weather floor liners and a cargo tray
Apple CarPlay / Android Auto head unit on pre-2020 cars that lacked it
Mild appearance touches (wheels, window tint) — the enthusiast scene is small outside the GR Corolla
Honest take: the Corolla is about dependability and running costs, not speed — money is better spent on tires and maintenance than on chasing power
oil_type: 0W-16 full synthetic (0W-20 acceptable on many trims — check the cap)

generations.11th Gen E170 (2014–2019 US): The value-focused Corolla — 1.8L (132–140 hp), CVT or a 6-speed manual early on. Roomy back seat, very cheap to run, if a bit dull to drive.
generations.12th Gen E210 (2020–present US): A big step up on the TNGA-C platform — sharper handling, a proper 2.0L Dynamic Force option (169 hp), a much better interior, and a genuinely efficient 1.8L hybrid. Sedan and hatchback body styles; Toyota Safety Sense standard.
generations.Note: The high-performance GR Corolla (three-cylinder turbo, AWD) is a separate enthusiast model, not part of the mainstream Corolla lineup covered here.

common_issues: 2020 Denso low-pressure fuel-pump recall — industry-wide across many makes, not Corolla-specific; verify it is closed by VIN
The CVT droning under hard acceleration — efficient but not sporty; the 2.0L with the launch gear feels more natural
Modest power, especially with the 1.8L and a full car — this is a commuter, not a quick car
Road and wind noise on the highway, more so on the lighter/base trims
Early E210 infotainment could feel dated; later cars improved with wireless CarPlay/Android Auto
maintenance_tips: Keep up with the specified low-viscosity synthetic oil on the Maintenance Minder — this engine asks for little else
Service the CVT fluid with genuine Toyota CVT fluid around 60k miles despite 'lifetime' claims — it is cheap insurance for a long-lived transmission
Confirm the fuel-pump recall and any open recalls by VIN before buying
Otherwise it is cabin filters, brake fluid, and tires — parts are cheap and available everywhere
The hybrid's traction battery is long-lived; just keep the 12V battery healthy, as a weak one causes odd electrical gremlins

engine.detail: 1.8L or 2.0L Dynamic Force four, or a 1.8L hybrid - port/direct-injection engines with a timing chain, so there's no belt to replace.
engine.watch: Very reliable; just keep up with the specified low-viscosity synthetic oil. Nothing chronic goes wrong with these engines.

drivetrain.detail: FWD with a CVT (a Direct-Shift CVT with a real launch gear on the 2.0L), an e-CVT on the hybrid, or a 6-speed manual on the 2.0L.
drivetrain.watch: One of the more durable CVTs in the class; change the fluid around 60k despite 'lifetime' claims. It drones under hard acceleration but rarely fails.

fuel.detail: Regular unleaded with port/direct injection and an in-tank electric fuel pump.
fuel.watch: Confirm the 2020 Denso low-pressure fuel-pump recall is closed by VIN - industry-wide, not Corolla-specific; a bad pump can stall the car.

electrical.detail: 12V battery, Toyota Safety Sense driver aids, and a touchscreen infotainment system.
electrical.watch: Early E210 infotainment felt dated (later cars got wireless CarPlay/Android Auto); a weak 12V battery causes odd gremlins, especially on the hybrid.
